newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jardine Fleming source says Smith to resign.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Fleming source says Smith to resign.

text.p: Alan Smith will resign as chairman of fund management company Jardine Fleming Holdings Ltd on Thursday, company sources said.
"I can confirm it," a Jardine Fleming source said.
Jardine Fleming will issue a statement at 3 p.m. (0700 GMT) announcing Smith's resignation, he said.
Smith is on vacation and unavailable for comment, his secretary said.
The source had no comment on reports that Robert Thomas would also resign as director of the company, which operates a number of securities businesses including fund management.
He also declined to speculate on whether the resignations were linked to a recent scandal involving the company's fund management practices in Hong Kong and London.

Thomas lost his registration with the British investment watchdog, the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation, and resigned as managing director of subsidiaries Jardine Fleming Investment Management and Jardine Fleming Asset Management following revelations last month of irregular trading practices.

Colin Armstrong, a fund manager at Hong Kong-based Jardine Fleming Investment Management, delayed processing deals, allowing for changes in the trading price. Some of the deals involved his personal account, regulators said.

IMRO fined Jardine Fleming 700,000 stg and revoked the authorisation of Jardine Fleming Asset Management in London. Jardine Fleming volunteered to pay an additional US$19.3 million to disadvantaged clients.
The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) in Hong Kong issued a public reprimand to the company and revoked Thomas' registration.
On the day the penalties were announced, Alan Smith made a public request for clients to "look at this going forward."
Jardine Fleming Investment Management, one of the largest fund companies in Asia with US$22 billion under management, now had a new emphasis on dealing and compliance procedures, he said.

"This incident is regrettable and we've expressed regret for it," Smith said on August 29. "Clearly as a result of this incident we've conducted a major review and we have a new emphasis on dealing and compliance procedures."
Company officials confirmed that a statement would be released at 0700 GMT but declined to comment on its contents.
Jardine Fleming is jointly held by Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd and Robert Fleming group.
